perspective:
I, Christian Mensah, have access to the following:

- I am a police officer and Jonathan Balogun’s childhood best friend. We have a strong bond; I often seek his advice, and I know he has a master’s degree and often offers a different perspective.
- I noticed Jonathan acting differently and came to feel he was hiding something important. This made me anxious and suspicious, so I arranged to meet him at our favorite coffee shop.
- At the meeting, I told Jonathan I felt he was hiding something. He admitted he had been keeping something from me because he didn’t want to worry me; he said he was in some trouble and didn’t know how to tell me.
- I felt worried and empathetic. I offered to help and said we could face it together. Jonathan said the situation was complicated and he didn’t want to drag me into it. I insisted he was my best friend and asked what he needed. He said he could use support and resources and needed to figure a way out of the mess.
- I asked if his trouble was related to anything illegal. Jonathan said he couldn’t say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he didn’t do anything illegal himself. I said I would look into it discreetly. He thanked me and said he trusted me to handle it carefully.
- Through my investigation, I came to believe Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up. I told him this. He asked if I was sure and who would do it. I said I wasn’t sure yet but had leads and would gather more evidence to prove his innocence.
- Later, I believed I found out who was behind it: someone close to both of us whom we know and trust. I told Jonathan I had found out who it was and planned to confront them and make sure they were brought to justice. Jonathan warned me this person is dangerous but said he trusted me to do what’s right.

I do not have access to any hidden events or private information beyond what I observed, was told, or learned through my own investigation.
